authoredFrom: SQL-D30, 2026-10-21. The bare-name self-edge guard in `addRelationship` dropped a `contains` edge whose source and target NAMES were equal — but a table and one of its columns may legally share a name, and then they are two declarations, two kinds (`class` and `property`) and two ids (`d30_keyword` and `d30_keyword.keyword`), which a name test cannot tell apart. MEASURED over the whole admitted population (PATHS 2,131 · DISTINCT 2,131 · ADMITTED 2,125, 199 symlinked directories FOLLOWED, 0 parse failures): the before/after with the grammar handed to BOTH analyzers is distinct edges 31,630 -> 31,639, delta +9, REMOVED 0 — the nine edges are `contains useragent -> install.sql::useragent.useragent` (cloogle.org/db/install.sql), `contains keyword -> schema.sql::keyword.keyword`, `contains name -> schema.sql::name.name` and `contains title -> schema.sql::title.title` (duckdb/benchmark/imdb_plan_cost/init/schema.sql), `contains adresse -> big_schema.sql::adresse.adresse` and `contains message -> big_schema.sql::message.message` (postgrest/test/io/fixtures/big_schema.sql), and `contains being -> schema.sql::being.being`, `contains descendant -> schema.sql::descendant.descendant` and `contains part -> schema.sql::part.part` (postgrest/test/spec/fixtures/schema.sql). THE FIXTURE IS RED-ABLE AGAINST THE COMMITTED ANALYZER: the two same-name edges are ABSENT there and PRESENT here, so a fixture that could not go red would not be a fixture.
comment: THE TWO RED ROWS ARE THE TWO TABLES WHOSE COLUMN SHARES THE TABLE'S OWN NAME — `d30_self` and `keyword` — and they are what the pre-fix analyzer dropped. The `keyword` table is the EXACT shape the differential measured as a MISSING row (duckdb/benchmark/imdb_plan_cost/init/schema.sql), so the fixture mirrors the corpus row rather than a paraphrase of it. THE NEGATIVE CONTROLS ARE TWO DIFFERENT QUESTIONS: `d30_keyword` carries a COLUMN named `keyword` under a table with a DIFFERENT name (so the old guard never fired there — a fix that stopped publishing keyword-named columns would fail this row), and `d30_distinct`/`d30_other` carry the ORDINARY shape (so a fix that stopped publishing containment edges altogether would fail these). THE SYMBOL ROWS MATTER AS MUCH AS THE EDGE ROWS: before the fix the column SYMBOL existed while its containment edge did not, so a consumer reading the graph saw a column that belonged to no table — and `expectSymbolCount` pins the same-name fact from the SYMBOL side: `d30_self` appears TWICE (once as the table, once as the column of that table), `keyword` appears once as a TABLE and once as the column of the table `keyword` and once as the column of the table `d30_keyword` — three distinct declarations sharing one name, which is exactly the population the bare-name test could not tell apart. THE `contains` COUNT IS 9, not 6: the fixture declares NINE columns across five tables (d30_self 2 · keyword 2 · d30_keyword 2 · d30_distinct 2 · d30_other 1).
